searchText: The fear is that presigned cold wallet transfers will break. One suggestion was to introduce a precompile where you could submit old format transactions. Sort of like EIP-3074, but specifically legacy signed transactions. It is unknown if there exist any such presigned transactions, but it would be a not-unreasonable tiered security model. Well, we could keep it allowed and only disable forwarding them Then if you really really want, you could inject it into a miner to have it mined Do we get meaningful gains making them minable but not gossipable? It would mean that if you want to get a non-EIP155 transaction on the chain, you'd have to jump through extra hoops, so that ensures that this actor **really** wants to get their non-EIP155 transaction mined. So that also ensures that this actor really has a good reason for it (because they will know that they are explicitly putting this non-EIP155 transaction on chain, and thus also should have some level of technical knowledge) I mean what benefits do we have by making it hard for users to send legacy transactions? Does it help us reduce technical debt in some way? Geth doesn't make it hard to send legacy transactions, it makes it hard to send non-EIP155 legacy transactions Ah, the idea is to protect users? If so, I don't think the clients are the right place to do that. Really that sort of protection should be done by wallets. Agreed, unfortunately some wallets still used non-EIP155 signed transactions. That's why we decided that it would be time to gently nudge them to start using them There are legitimate use cases for cross-chain replayable transactions. Relatively few, but I'm not a fan of disabling transmission without some benefit (besides doing a job someone else should be doing). I agree, however I don't think these use cases outweigh the cost of users getting rekt/griefed by using a side-chain / L2 What do side chains/L2s have to do with this? People keep using their accounts across different chains Has this resulted in real problems, or only theoretic? https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-2315-simple-subroutines-for-the-evm/3941/105 Yeah, Avax went offline for 3 days because of it 😄 The bridge used non protected transactions and certain users figured out they can loop-withdraw, or something Arguably not Ethereum's or clients' fault Still feels like "not a Geth problem". but still, nobody expected it I would favor removing legacy transaction gossip support sometime after 1559 lands, as that would allow clients to cleanup (in theory) some code. I'm just a bit leery of encouraging client devs do *more* work because some people messed up on security. Of course, client devs can do whatever they want, I just don't think it is the best use of time. 🙂 I heard the 'wink, wink' and as a tool maker I want to add support to TrueBlocks. I believe there's another change with the new wrapped transactions. Are there other changes? Is there a document for tool makers somewhere detailing what changes might be expected from the RPC or is reading EIPs the best source?
